title: Let Execution Do the Teaching
abstract: arXiv:2611.19875v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Improving a coding model is a sequence of decisions: find the limiting behavior, create useful practice, and determine which attempts deserve reinforcement. We investigate a practical way to make those decisions increasingly repeatable by grounding feedback in execution. Starting from GLM-4.7-Flash, the work combines whole-file supervised fine-tuning, targeted C++ repair curricula, group-relative reinforcement learning, and verifiers that turn program behavior into structured rewards. Compiler errors and failing tests provide specific contexts for repair practice, while executable checks score the resulting programs. We evaluate the trained models on 26 C++ coding tasks, measuring both initial success and completion after test feedback. The strongest reported post-training configuration achieves 45.2% success in the first test round and 61.5% within two rounds. These results come from an assisted development suite with evolving prompt

translated_abstract: 改进一个编程模型是一系列决策过程：找出限制性能的行为、创建有用的练习、并确定哪些尝试值得强化。我们研究了一种实用的方法，通过将反馈建立在程序执行之上，使这些决策愈发可重复。该工作从 GLM-4.7-Flash 出发，结合了整文件监督微调、针对性的 C++ 修复课程、组相对强化学习，以及能将程序行为转化为结构化奖励的验证器。编译器错误和未通过的测试为修复练习提供了具体的上下文，而可执行的检查则对生成的程序进行评分。我们在 26 个 C++ 编程任务上评估了训练后的模型，同时衡量初始成功率和在测试反馈后的完成率。所报告的最强后训练配置在第一轮测试中达到 45.2% 的成功率，在两轮内达到 61.5%。这些结果来自一个配有持续演进提示词的辅助开发套件。
tldr: 该论文提出以程序执行结果为核心训练信号的方法，将编译错误与测试反馈融入监督微调、C++修复课程和组相对强化学习中，并借助执行验证器生成结构化奖励，使 GLM-4.7-Flash 在 C++ 编程任务上的两轮成功率提升至 61.5%。
en_tdlr: This paper grounds coding-model training in program execution—combining whole-file SFT, targeted C++ repair curricula, and group-relative RL with execution-based verifiers that turn compiler errors and test outcomes into structured rewards—raising GLM-4.7-Flash's success rate on 26 C++ tasks to 61.5% within two feedback rounds.
